image_description: A close-up view of a large whale breaching or surfacing in dark ocean water. The whale has a dark grey, mottled skin with white patches (barnacles/callosities) on its head and rostrum. Notably, there is a bright orange, cone-shaped object attached to the side of the whale's body near the blowhole area, which appears artificial. The background consists of choppy sea water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rostrum is visible and arched, but the blowholes are obscured by the angle and the orange object; furthermore, the head shape resembles a Humpback more than a Grey Whale due to the tubercles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture and coloration match the description of a baleen whale with callosities/barnacles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The posterior back and dorsal region are not visible in this cropped shot of the head/shoulders.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior portion of the body is visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed; baleen plates are internal and not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Tail flukes are outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visible white patches on the head indicate rough texture/callosities consistent with baleen whales.

artifact_observations.location: Right side of the whale's head/neck area
artifact_observations.reasoning: There is a bright orange, geometric cone-shaped object attached to the whale. This is physically implausible for a wild animal and suggests an AI generation error where a buoy or marker was fused into the animal's flesh, or a 'hallucinated' object that lacks realistic attachment mechanics (no straps, seamless fusion).

artifact_observations.location: Interface between orange object and whale skin
artifact_observations.reasoning: The boundary between the orange object and the wet skin is slightly soft and lacks the distinct shadowing or displacement of water/skin that would occur if a rigid object were pressed against a moving whale.

selected_experts.reason: To verify if the species is actually a Grey Whale or if it is a Humpback (which has similar callosities but different head shape), and to detect if the image is a composite.
To analyze the physical plausibility of the orange object's attachment and check for melting/fusion artifacts at the boundary.
To ensure the whale is a single coherent entity and the orange object is either part of the topology (error) or a separate distinct object.
To identify what the orange object is supposed to be (buoy, tag, etc.) to assess semantic consistency.

Boundary integrity between the object and the skin
